guide: Open Start and type your center name, your wanted occupancy, your staff pay limit, your wanted margin, your cash floor and your owner draw in the yellow cells. These are your own targets: check your local rules for anything the law sets.
Check Rooms and Rates. They hold the licensed places, the ratio and the weekly rate of each room and schedule that the other sheets look up.

Each month enter one row in Profit and Loss: tuition and fee revenue, staff pay, owner pay, food, rent, other costs, paid staff hours and child-days. Revenue, costs, profit and the shares fill in by themselves.
Enter one row per room and month in Room Profit by Month: children, revenue, staff cost, food cost and the overhead share. Profit, occupancy and the children still needed to break even fill in.
Enter the cash in and out each month in Cash by Month. The closing balance and the margin over your cash floor fill in by themselves.
Enter every expense in Expenses with a category and every bill in Bills. Budget against Actual compares them with your budget; rows without a category show in the category check.
Add the child-hours attended in Cost per Child-Hour. Fee Check by Room then shows the cost and the fee of a child-hour in each room.
Use Break-even by Month, Occupancy by Month and Staff Cost Share to see where the center stands against your own targets.
Read Tax Set-aside and Owner Draw Plan for the next 12 months. The set-aside is a planning figure: confirm tax amounts and dates with your adviser.
A single home daycare provider fills Home-use Share Lines: choose rooms, hours or both for each cost line and ask your adviser to confirm. Keep one row in Rooms.
Open Year in Review to see this period against the period before, with a verdict for each measure.
Use the 18 calculators to test break-even, fees, the loss-making room, your draw, the budget, sensitivity, cash runway and a new group of children.
Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and tap a message link to send a text with the figures already written in.
Read the Owner Dashboard and the charts every month: revenue, costs, profit, occupancy, staff pay share, cash and the room that loses money.

listing.title: Childcare Center Business Health Excel Template: Profit and Loss, Break-Even Occupancy, Room Profit, Cost per Child-Hour, Cash Flow
listing.headline: Know which room earns, what break-even is and what you can draw
listing.description:
Run the money side of a home daycare or childcare center in one Excel workbook. Built for an owner-director and an assistant director who want one clear view of profit, break-even and cash. Profit and Loss holds the month: tuition and fee revenue, staff pay, owner pay, food, rent and other costs, with profit, margin and the staff pay share worked out for you. Room Profit by Month shows revenue, staff cost, food cost and the overhead share of every room, so the room that loses money is easy to see and so are the children it needs to break even.

Cost per Child-Hour and Fee Check by Room set the fee of a child-hour against its cost. Break-even by Month gives the break-even children and the break-even occupancy (children booked as a share of licensed places). Budget against Actual compares your budget with your expenses by category. Cash by Month, Tax Set-aside and the Owner Draw Plan show the cash, the income tax set-aside and your draw for the next 12 months, with a floor you choose. Year in Review sets this period against the one before and marks each measure stronger, steady or weaker.

18 calculators answer the questions an owner asks: enrol two more infants or lose a family, is a fee right, which room loses, is the draw affordable, how long does cash last, is a new group worth opening. Home-use Share Lines help a single home daycare provider turn rooms or hours into cost lines. Print 12 sheets and 12 documents, follow 12 checklists and send 34 ready text messages to the owner-director, the assistant director, the accountant, lead teachers and suppliers.

This is part eight of the Home Daycare and Childcare Center suite. A standard .xlsx workbook with no macros and no subscription, with a demo copy full of sample data to explore first. Children appear by name, room and dates only, with no medical detail. It helps you keep track of your business and does not promise results. Confirm tax and set-aside figures with your adviser and check your local rules.

competitors.lacks: list income and costs but never turn them into break-even children, cost per child-hour or a profit figure for each room
charge every month for reports that hide the overhead rule, so you cannot test whether a room really loses money
know revenue and costs but not rooms, places, ratios, child-hours, the staff pay share or a quarterly owner draw
arrive months late and show last year, with no scenario for enrolling two more infants or losing a family
record what came in and out but give no cash floor, no runway and no set-aside plan for the next 12 months

documents.title: Budget against actual for one category
paragraphs: Budget against actual of {set:company}, dated {today}. Category {col:budget.category}, month {col:budget.month}.
Budget {col:budget.budget}, actual {col:budget.actual}, variance {col:budget.variance}, which is {col:budget.var_pct} of the budget. Budget check: {col:budget.flag}.

Over the last 12 months this category had a budget of {col:budget.cat_budget} and an actual of {col:budget.cat_actual}, a variance of {col:budget.cat_var}. It ranks {col:budget.rank_over} for overspend and {col:budget.rank_spend} for spend.
Write below what you will check or change.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own center and check your local rules.

documents.title: Owner draw and tax set-aside plan for one month
paragraphs: Owner draw and set-aside plan of {set:company}, dated {today}. Month: {col:draw_plan.month}.

Profit before the draw {col:draw_plan.forecast}. Owner draw {col:draw_plan.draw}. Profit after the draw {col:draw_plan.profit_after}. Income tax set-aside {col:draw_plan.set_aside}. Extra draw {col:draw_plan.extra_draw}.
Cash change {col:draw_plan.net_cash}. Cash left {col:draw_plan.cash_left}, against your floor of {set:cash_floor}. Cash check: {col:draw_plan.floor_flag}.
The set-aside is a planning figure. Please confirm tax amounts and dates with your adviser. Check your local rules.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own center and check your local rules.

documents.title: Home-use share worksheet for one cost line
paragraphs: Home-use share worksheet of {set:company}, dated {today}. Cost line: {col:home_lines.line}.

Whole-house amount a month {col:home_lines.amount}. Rule: {col:home_lines.rule}. Business share {col:home_lines.share}. Business amount a month {col:home_lines.business_amount}, a year {col:home_lines.yearly_amount}.

The rooms used for the business are {set:home_rooms_used} of {set:home_rooms_total}, used {set:home_hours_used} hours of {set:home_hours_week} hours a week. Set on {col:home_lines.set_on}. Status: {col:home_lines.status}.
This worksheet turns rooms or hours into cost lines. It does not decide what you may claim: please confirm every line with your adviser and check your local rules.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own center and check your local rules.

documents.title: Year in review for one measure
paragraphs: Year in review of {set:company}, dated {today}. Review period: {col:year_review.basis}.

Measure: {col:year_review.measure}. This period {col:year_review.this_period}. Period before {col:year_review.last_period}. Change {col:year_review.change}, which is {col:year_review.change_pct} of the period before.
Verdict: {col:year_review.verdict}. A change within {set:steady_band} counts as steady. Costs and staff pay share are better when they fall.
Write below what you keep, what you change and what you plan for the next period.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own center and check your local rules.

documents.title: Accountant pack with profit and loss and cash for one month
paragraphs: Accountant pack of {set:company}, dated {today}. Month: {col:cash.month}. Prepared for {col:cash.accountant}.

Cash: opening {col:cash.opening}, parent payments {col:cash.parent_payments}, government payments {col:cash.government_payments}, pay out {col:cash.pay_out}, expenses out {col:cash.expenses_out}, income tax set aside {col:cash.tax_set_aside}, deposit refunds {col:cash.deposit_refunds}, owner extra draw {col:cash.owner_extra}.
Closing cash {col:cash.closing}, a change of {col:cash.net_change} in the month and {col:cash.above_floor} above your floor. Cash check: {col:cash.floor_flag}.
Attach the monthly profit and loss, the expense list and the bills due. Please confirm tax treatment and dates with your adviser.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own center and check your local rules.

documents.title: Equipment purchase case for one expense
paragraphs: Equipment purchase case of {set:company}, dated {today}. Expense {col:expenses.expense_id} on {col:expenses.date}.

Item: {col:expenses.description}. Category: {col:expenses.category}. Amount: {col:expenses.amount}. Paid to: {col:expenses.paid_to}. This is {col:expenses.share_of_category} of the spend in this category over 12 months.
Reason for the purchase, the extra places or the saving it brings, and the months to pay back: write them below. Cash must stay above your floor of {set:cash_floor}.
Decision: buy now, wait or decline.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own center and check your local rules.

documents.sheet: Annual Plan for the Next Year
documents.title: Annual plan with break-even and occupancy by month
paragraphs: Annual plan of {set:company}, dated {today}. Month used as the base: {col:breakeven.month}.

Children enrolled {col:breakeven.children} of {col:breakeven.places} places, an occupancy of {col:breakeven.occupancy}. Fixed costs {col:breakeven.fixed_costs}. Revenue per child {col:breakeven.revenue_child}. Food cost per child {col:breakeven.variable_child}.
Break-even children {col:breakeven.be_children}, a break-even occupancy of {col:breakeven.be_occupancy}. Cushion over break-even {col:breakeven.cushion}. Check: {col:breakeven.position}.
Write below the occupancy you plan, the fee changes, the budget and the owner draw for the next year.
documents.note: Sample wording: adapt it to your own center and check your local rules.

documents.title: Fee setting note for a room and schedule
paragraphs: Fee note of {set:company}, dated {today}. Room {col:rates.room}, schedule {col:rates.schedule}.

The weekly rate is {col:rates.weekly_rate} and the weekly rate for your wanted margin is {col:rates.needed_rate}. A rise of {col:rates.rise_needed} would reach it. Last year the rate rose by {col:rates.rise_pct}.
Notice of a fee rise is given to families in writing before it starts: check your contract terms and your local rules. The yearly fee review is on {col:rates.review_date}.
Fees are before any tax. Write the new rate and the date it starts below.
